subtype: Approach: fear of missing out drives a quick decision [Pitfall]
passage: In the office pantry, Francis scrolled through a tip group where screenshots of gains kept arriving. Colleagues had said they were doubling money in a week. Someone posted "last chance today, closing in one hour". Francis felt the hurry rise in the chest, did not check who ran the group, and moved the whole month's savings to the account given. Ten minutes later the group went silent and the admin left. Sumit from accounts found Francis staring at the phone and said, "Show me." The screenshots were the same picture with different names. Sumit walked Francis to the desk phone and they called the bank's fraud line together, then filed the report on the official cybercrime portal. The money could not be recovered.

qa.q: How much time did the last chance message say was left?
qa.a: The message said the group was closing in one hour.

qa.q: What was Francis feeling when moving the savings?
qa.a: Francis felt a rush of hurry and fear of missing out, and did not stop to check who ran the group.

qa.q: What could Francis do differently next time, and why?
qa.a: Francis could pause for a day, ask who runs the group and talk to a trusted person, because urgency and social proof are used to stop checking.

qa.q: How might Sumit see the situation?
qa.a: Sumit likely feels concerned for Francis and acts quickly by phoning the bank's fraud line and helping to report it.

grounding: Seeing others post gains, a young worker rushes into a tip group and transfers savings within an hour, and the money cannot be recovered.

subtype: Approach: fear of missing out drives a quick decision [Pitfall]
passage:
Dear Lalremsiami,
You asked why I've been so quiet since Holi. Here it is, because I'd rather you hear it from me.
That Saturday, three people from my office batch posted screenshots of their gains, ₹12,000, ₹20,000, all from a tip group on a chat app. One of them wrote, 'Last day for new members.' I joined at 9:40 p.m. By 10:30 I had sent ₹45,000, most of my savings from eighteen months of work. I didn't check who ran the group. I didn't ask anyone. It felt like everyone else was already on the train and it was leaving.
Two days later the group vanished. The bank says the money went to an account that has already been emptied. I reported it to the cybercrime helpline, but they told me honestly that recovery is unlikely.
I'm writing so you don't do what I did.
Bhavna

qa.a: ₹45,000, most of Bhavna's savings from eighteen months of work.

qa.q: What was Bhavna feeling that Saturday night?
qa.a: Bhavna felt panicked about being left out, as if everyone was on a train that was leaving, which shut out any checking.

qa.q: What could Bhavna have done at 9:40 p.m. instead?
qa.a: Waited a day and asked someone trusted, or checked who ran the group, since 'last day' pressure is itself a warning sign.

qa.q: How might Lalremsiami feel reading the letter?
qa.a: Sad for Bhavna and grateful for the honesty, and more wary of screenshots of gains. 🤍

grounding: Shows a young worker rushing into a tip group after seeing friends' gains, sending savings within an hour and being unable to recover them.

subtype: Approach: fear of missing out drives a quick decision [Pitfall]
passage:
Manoj, you asked why I still don't have a bike. Okay. I'm Hrithik, and I lost my bike money in about fifty minutes.
It was after a match. Everyone in our cricket group was posting screenshots from a tip group on a chat app. Profits. Green numbers. Someone wrote, 'Only ten slots left tonight.' My heart was racing. I joined, and the admin messaged me within a minute: 'Send now, trading opens at 8.' I sent ₹30,000 from my savings. Didn't call my dad, didn't search anything. Just sent it.
Next morning the group had a new name and I'd been removed. My number blocked.
I did go to the bank that same day, and filed a complaint on the cybercrime portal. They're looking into it, but they said it's hard. So yeah, Manoj. That's where the bike went. Next time someone says 'only ten slots', I'm going to think of this.

qa.q: How did Hrithik feel when the 'only ten slots' message came?
qa.a: Hrithik felt a rush of panic and excitement, heart racing, afraid of missing out.

qa.q: What would have slowed Hrithik down at that moment?
qa.a: Calling a parent or searching the group before sending anything; the 'ten slots' pressure was meant to stop exactly that.

qa.q: What might Manoj take from hearing this?
qa.a: Manoj hears a friend's honest loss and might think twice the next time screenshots and slot counts appear in a group.

grounding: Shows a young worker pushed by friends' screenshots and a slot deadline into sending savings within the hour, money that cannot be recovered.
